anthropic.markdown:
## v1.14.0 — 2026-03-26

This release focuses on production hardening and security improvements, introducing webhook idempotency, metrics gating, audit logging, email throttling, and enhanced security headers. Key infrastructure improvements include better error handling, Alpine Linux compatibility fixes, and production deployment hardening for Railway hosting.

### ✨ Features

- Added webhook idempotency to prevent duplicate processing of webhook requests
- Implemented metrics gating for controlled access to application metrics
- Added audit logging functionality for security and compliance tracking
- Implemented email throttling to prevent spam and abuse
- Added 404 error page for better user experience
- Implemented X-Request-Id header for request tracing
- Added Content Security Policy (CSP) headers for enhanced security
- Implemented Progressive Web App (PWA) capabilities

### 🔧 Improvements

- Softened production startup checks to warnings instead of hard failures
- Increased healthcheck timeout from default to 30 seconds for better reliability
- Completed and optimized Dockerfile for production deployment

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed Alpine Linux crash by removing static @sentry/node import and reducing 64 dependencies
- Added try/catch guard around migrate() function to prevent startup failures
- Modified health check to return 200 status even when database is degraded
- Hardened Railway deployment with 0.0.0.0 binding and faster database timeout
- Fixed release patch ordering to display in ascending order

### 🧹 Chores

- Simplified CI pipeline by removing redundant launch-readiness checks and using single Node 22 version
- Retagged all releases for correct semantic versioning and filled v1.1 gap
- Optimized pre-push hooks for faster development workflow

### Contributors

@mttaylor

gemini.markdown:
## v1.14.0 — 2026-03-26

This release delivers significant production hardening, security enhancements, and new features. Key improvements include robust security measures such as webhook idempotency and audit logging, enhanced production readiness with features like a custom 404 page and CSP headers, and critical fixes addressing deployment stability, health checks, and dependency issues.

### ✨ Features

- Introduced production readiness features such as a custom 404 page, X-Request-Id header for request tracing, enhanced metrics, Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, additional tests, and Progressive Web App (PWA) capabilities.

### 🔧 Improvements

- Implemented security hardening measures including webhook idempotency, metrics gating, audit logging, email throttling, and draft tests.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Hardened Railway deployments by ensuring the application binds to 0.0.0.0, setting a faster database connection timeout, and completing the Dockerfile configuration.
- Improved application resilience by guarding the migrate() function with a try/catch block and ensuring the health check returns a 200 status even when degraded.
- Resolved an Alpine crash by removing the static import of @sentry/node and reduced the dependency footprint by 64 packages.
- Improved production startup robustness by softening critical startup checks to warnings and increasing the health check timeout to 30 seconds.

### 🧹 Chores

- Retagged all releases to ensure correct semantic versioning and filled a gap in the v1.1 release series.
- Simplified CI pipelines by removing redundant launch-readiness checks, standardizing on a single Node 22 environment, and implementing faster pre-push hooks.

### Contributors

@mttaylor
